{
  "items": [
    {
      "id": "AJCR.w4-rep",
      "title": "Wave 4: representability of Pic^0 (curve-specialised Kleiman)",
      "projects": [
        "Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild"
      ],
      "summary": "================================================================================
CURRENT STATE, READ THIS FIRST (review-ajcr r4, 2026-07-30). Everything below
this block is the audit HISTORY: five layers of correction and self-correction,
in which the actual costing does not appear until roughly halfway down. It is
kept because each retraction is evidence, but a lane picking a target should
read this block and then jump to the header "THE COSTING, RE-RANKED".
================================================================================

THE MACHINE IS SOUND AND HAS NOTHING TO FEED IT. pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy
(Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are sorry-free, kernel-confirmed, non-circular,
and WOULD produce a representing scheme. All three antecedents are undischarged
and no sorry-free witness exists for any of them.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS, ranked by measured cost, cheapest last:
 1. IsChartUniv (the per-index chart certificate, `hf`) -- CERT-Sigma-gated.
    Refuted at V = top and free-but-useless at V = bot; whether the PAIR holds at
    any V strictly between is UNMEASURED at every V. Inhabitation at one concrete
    V is the open question. Rows: chart-u, chart-restrict, atlas-coupling.
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc f (DAT-B coverage) -- the most
    expensive, and multi-round (told to the human as I-1090). Cannot be discounted
    by restricting the atlas: ajcr-p1's isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_mono carries
    any V up to top, where the inclusion is an iso. Restricted coverage is no
    cheaper than unrestricted -- and note only ONE direction is proved, so it is
    as measured STRICTLY STRONGER. Row: dat-b.
 3. rep i (a representation of divFunctor at each parameter) -- the divisor-
    representability lane's target. Rows: ddr.divrep (+ u2, abel-widened).

RIDERS THAT ARE NOT SEPARATE OBLIGATIONS, both established by retraction below:
 * hD (LocallyOfFiniteType) is a rider on antecedent 3, proved via
   rep.uniqueUpToIso -- unconditional, not contingent on the carrier divRep
   returns.
 * hcpt IS the JacobianData.quasiCompact field, so dat-glue and dat-j name ONE
   obligation. Qualification (r4, I-1162): the half carrying that -- the mpr
   direction -- has been the producer's own implementation since 07-27
   (JacobianDataCharts.lean:216); the new content is the mp direction, which
   shows the identification cannot be undone. hcl still has no producer, so
   nothing there is discharged.

r4 REPRICING -- WITHDRAWN BY ITS AUTHOR, same session. I wrote here that the chart
parameter n is pinned to the genus by chi_moduleKSheaf UNCONDITIONALLY, so
abel-noninj owed no "we are at n = g" argument and its n > g branch was
unreachable. FALSE, refuted by a fresh-context audit (I-1176) and reproduced:
chi_moduleKSheaf CONVERTS chi = 1 - n into n = genus C, it does not SUPPLY
chi = 1 - n. With n free and no chi hypothesis the goal FAILS, and it still fails
with a representation at n in scope. My probe had hchi as a binder, so it measured
the conversion (I-1177).
   THE STANDING PRICE is ajcr-p2's: n > g is unreachable for a chart built on a
producer IN THIS TREE, because each such producer carries an hchi at its own
index. That is a claim about producers and a lane must keep them in view.
Whether an inhabitant exists at n != genus C is an OPEN inhabitation question
about DivRepAffinePullback -- mixedParamChart typechecks at arbitrary nn.
abel-noninj's live target is unchanged: the carve question, does DivScheme g
contain points where H^1 fails to vanish.

SORRY COUNT IS NOT DEBT HERE: 17 sorries, all in Challenge.lean (15, the
statement-only north star) and Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean (2). A naive count reads
AJCR as nearly done. It is not -- the gap is the three antecedents above, none of
which is a sorry.

ANSWER TO THE COSTING QUESTION, unchanged this round: none of the three closes
this week (human-facing accounting at I-0984). The items where a single round can
still produce a DECISIVE result rather than partial progress are antecedent 1's
inhabitation at one concrete V, and the abel-noninj carve question now that its
degree is pinned.

================================================================================
HISTORY FOLLOWS -- corrections in reverse chronological layers.
================================================================================

*** hcpt CLAUSE RETRACTED 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006), refuted by ajcr-p4 (I-1007)
within minutes of my writing it. THE DEGENERACY OBSERVATION IS REAL; MY CAUSAL READING WAS
CONFOUNDED. ***

I wrote, in the self-correction below, that "hcpt is NOT an independent gate but a CONSEQUENCE of
coverage", inferred from hcpt being free at iota := PEmpty while all content sat in the
IsLocallySurjective instance. p4's refutation is decisive and I verified its pivot myself (EXIT=0):
PEmpty IS FINITE. So freeness of hcpt there is explained by the FINITE-INDEX route
(JacobianData.ofCharts with per-chart compactness at an empty cover), with coverage contributing
nothing. A degenerate index attributes to whichever hypothesis happens to vary, and I varied the
wrong one.

WHAT p4 MEASURED, more useful than my claim was: feeding the openCover route directly,
(glueData hf).openCover.compactSpace fails on EXACTLY ONE goal --
Finite (glueData hf).openCover.I0. Not chart compactness, not the cover being a cover, not
coverage. Add [Finite iota] plus per-chart CompactSpace and the same term closes. p4 also applies my
own I-0978 correctly: a failing synthesis measures the instance graph, so this does NOT prove hcpt
independent of coverage -- it shows no route in scope derives it, and the single gap on the
available route is INDEX FINITENESS, which the class-indexed atlas provably lacks.

CONSEQUENCE, and it strengthens the item rather than weakening it: DO NOT schedule "derive hcpt
from coverage". The two honest options are the ones the tree names -- a finite atlas, or the Abel
image (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage out of a quasi-compact DivScheme). The class-indexed atlas
needs the second, and PRICING IT is the unowned work. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-j points there.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006, after a fresh-context
review of my OWN correction below). THE FOURTH ITEM IS NOT AN ANTECEDENT AT ALL -- IT IS A RIDER
ON antecedent 3, AND I PROVED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT. Read this before the arithmetic
correction that follows; that correction's CONCLUSION survives but its UNIT OF PRICING was wrong. ***

WHAT I GOT RIGHT AND WHAT I GOT WRONG. Right: the count was 3-of-3 where the goal needs more, the
"derived, not assumed" sentence was misleading, and ajcr-p4's discharge is real. WRONG: I priced
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom as a FOURTH INDEPENDENT ANTECEDENT that p4 removed,
and justified its cheapness by the CARRIER the divRep lane happens to return today
(locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom). That argument is CONTINGENT -- it would need re-measuring
if divRep ever returned a different object.

THE UNCONDITIONAL FACT, PROBED, `lake env lean` EXIT=0, axioms [propext, Classical.choice,
Quot.sound]: if divFunctor C pi n is representable by D and by D', and D'.hom is locally of finite
type, then D.hom is. Three lines -- e := rep.uniqueUpToIso rep', e.hom.left is IsIso via
Over.comp_left on hom_inv_id, then rw [<- Over.w e.hom] and infer_instance.

SO hD IS AN INVARIANT OF THE FUNCTOR AT THE PARAMETER, not a property of the chosen carrier. No
producer of rep can choose a D that fails it, and none can be blamed for one that does. The right
place for it on this board is as a RIDER ON THE rep ROW (divrep), not as an item of its own -- a
row that lists it separately INFLATES the antecedent count, which is the same error in the
opposite direction from the one I was correcting.

THE ANTECEDENT LIST OF THE GOAL, corrected again and now on unconditional grounds:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability -- CARRYING hD as a rider that costs its producer nothing.
    OPEN (divrep.u2).
 4. quasiCompact. OPEN, and see the degeneracy note below, which reprices it.

AND A DEGENERACY THAT REPRICES quasiCompact, measured on the same pass. At iota := PEmpty EVERY
explicit input of jacobianDataOfMixedParamCharts is free -- hf/hdeg/V/hD/m/Z/nn by PEmpty.elim,
and hcpt free too because an empty family glues to an EMPTY space (IsEmpty => CompactSpace by
inferInstance). ALL the content sits in the single IsLocallySurjective instance. The output is
nevertheless NOT vacuous, and that was also probed (EXIT=0, same axioms): that instance at PEmpty
implies False, because JacobianData.rep yields a point of J over every test (homEquiv.symm 1)
while J.left is empty. TWO CONSEQUENCES: (a) the assembly is sound and falsifiable, so nothing
here is a HasDivFunctor-style vacuity; (b) hcpt is NOT an independent gate of this shape but a
CONSEQUENCE of coverage -- and any future "hcpt discharged" measured at a small atlas measures
nothing at all.

ALSO CORRECTED, and it is a false absolute I repeated from p4's file: "the only declaration in
Picard/ whose conclusion is LocallyOfFiniteType is locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom". There are FIVE
non-local ones plus 38 local re-derivations; the omitted ones include the very instance
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199) that Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean imports and cites to make hD free, so the
absolute is refuted by that file's own closing section. THE DEFENSIBLE FORM, which is what a board
row should say: no producer AT A CHART. Same absolute is live on row
AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-glue.atlas-lft ("exactly ONE declaration") -- narrow it there too.

*** ARITHMETIC CORRECTION 2026-07-29 (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0006). THE ANTECEDENT COUNT ON THIS
ROW WAS THREE-OF-THREE WHERE THE GOAL NEEDS FOUR-OF-FOUR, AND ONE SENTENCE BELOW IS MISLEADING
IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS. Audited ajcr-p4's finding (I-0967/I-0977); it is CORRECT. ***

THE SENTENCE TO FIX IS MINE. Below, this row says the big-site sheaf condition, the 01JJ gluing
and "BOTH finiteness certificates -- which are DERIVED from chart-level hypotheses, not assumed"
are done and kernel-checked. Read against the statements that is wrong in effect: they are derived
from chart-level hypotheses THAT NOTHING IN THE TREE PRODUCED, which is not the same as derived.
locallyOfFiniteType_gluedHom (JacobianDataCharts.lean:154) TAKES
hlft : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (chartHom C f i); it was, until 67c8d24d5, the only Picard/
declaration concluding LocallyOfFiniteType at a chart, so the certificate was an assumption on
every route. PicRepDatum.lft (PicRepDatum.lean:100) is a structure FIELD -- also an assumption --
and toJacobianData (JacobianDataFromPicRepDatum.lean:87) only carries it across. So a lane that
discharged all THREE tracked antecedents would NOT have produced a JacobianData C, which is what
Challenge.lean's frozen Jacobian := (jacobianData C).J actually needs.

NOW DISCHARGED, AND IT IS A REAL DISCHARGE RATHER THAN A RELOCATION -- the part I checked hardest,
because "reduces to X" usually just moves the bill. Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean (ajcr-p4) proves
locallyOfFiniteType_chartHom_mixedParamChart: at the REAL atlas the certificate follows from
hD : forall i, LocallyOfFiniteType (D i).hom alone. And hD is FREE at the carrier the
divisor-representability lane returns: PROBED, imports current, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 --
LocallyOfFiniteType (divSchemeOver k A B g r1 r2 b1 b2).hom closes by inferInstance ALONE at
ARBITRARY window data, via the global instance locallyOfFiniteType_divSchemeOverHom
(DivSchemeQProj.lean:199), and DivOver (DivRepGlobalClassify.lean:113-116, :308) is an instance of
exactly that shape. So a lane producing rep supplies the fourth antecedent at the same moment at
zero cost.

WHAT REPLACES THE THREE-ITEM LIST, as the antecedent list of the GOAL:
 1. hf = IsChartUniv. OPEN (chart-restrict, ajcr-p1).
 2. Zariski-local surjectivity of Sigma.desc. OPEN (dat-b, ajcr-p2).
 3. rep i, divisor representability. OPEN (divrep.u2, ajcr-p3).
 4. hlft, chart finiteness. DISCHARGED at the real atlas, free at the rep carrier.
 5. quasiCompact. OPEN and GENUINELY A-POSTERIORI, and this is the item to watch now that 4 is
    gone. PER-CHART compactness is free at the same carrier (compactSpace_divScheme); CompactSpace
    of the GLUED object is not, and for the class-indexed (infinite) atlas the finite route
    JacobianData.ofCharts is unavailable, so it must come from the Abel image
    (JacobianData.ofChartsOfAbelImage). Do not let the freeness of the per-chart form be quoted
    for the glued form -- that conflation is exactly what this correction is about.

THE VERDICT IS UNCHANGED: none of the three OPEN antecedents closes this week (I-0873). Item 4
was never on the list, so removing it does not shorten the critical path; what it does is make
the remaining list the true one. One caveat on the discharging file itself:
Pic0AtlasFiniteType.lean:65 claims "everything in it other than hf, the local-surjectivity
instance and rep is now discharged", while hcpt is an explicit hypothesis of the same definition
and the file's own :184-186 and :262-265 call it open. The :262 reading is the correct one.

*** SELF-CORRECTION 2026-07-29, SAME SESSION (review-ajcr, run 0082 s0004, after a fresh-context
review of my own work). THE IsPlusHonest FINDING BELOW IS OVERSTATED ON THE STEP THAT CARRIES IT.
The route-decision conclusion SURVIVES, for a different and better-evidenced reason. ***

WHAT I GOT WRONG. I argued: relPicToPicEt lands in PicEtAff.unit, unit is mk at the TRIVIAL cover
`.self A` alone, therefore honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed. That step is
FALSE. PicEtAff.unit_eq_mk (Picard/RelPicCoverInjective.lean:48) proves a unit class is presented on
EVERY cover E, not only on `.self` -- so "mk at the trivial cover" describes one PRESENTATION, not
the RANGE, and nothing follows about which classes the range contains.

AND THE ABSOLUTE FORM IS REFUTED BY A LANDED THEOREM IN THIS TREE:
PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section (Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141) proves the unit SURJECTIVE
over a field test K admitting a curve point sigma, upgraded to a MulEquiv by
PicEtAff.unitEquiv_of_section (:186). Over such tests honesty is DISCHARGED OUTRIGHT -- vacuously
true, no etale cover needed anywhere. So "IsPlusHonest is the sheafification gap asserted of an
arbitrary section" is wrong as an absolute.

THE CORRECTED CLAIM, which is narrower and better supported. The gap is at a GENERAL AFFINE BASE
WITH NO SECTION, and the tree documents exactly why:
 * the field route closes only through etale-cover cofinality in finite separable field extensions
   (Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom, EtaleCover.lean:287) -- there is NO
   general-base analogue of that cofinality;
 * EffectivityMoving.lean:41-48 states plainly that for a merely quasi-finite (non-finite) etale
   cover the moving statement is FALSE, with a counterexample sketch (B = A_u x A_v over a
   2-dimensional normal local A with nontrivial local class group). So the [Module.Finite A B]
   hypothesis in the effectivity layer is load-bearing, not convenience.

SO THE OBSTRUCTION IS BASE-SHAPE, NOT ARBITRARINESS OF THE CLASS. Two consequences:
 1. the split to hand a prover lane is NOT "chart value (cheap) vs arbitrary section (blocked)" but
    "field test with a section (FREE) vs general sectionless affine base (OPEN)". The delta between
    the chart side and the coverage side is NARROWER than I priced it;
 2. antecedent 2 still owes a route decision -- which site coverage is local for -- because the
    repair still refines covers and descends, and Zariski-local surjectivity still will not absorb
    that. The conclusion stands; cite the module-finiteness counterexample, NOT the trivial-cover
    claim, when repeating it.

Also corrected, same review: I called DivisorFamilyAffThetaTyping.lean UNROOTED. It is ROOTED --
AlgebraicJacobian.lean:346 imports it at HEAD (commit 2b8cef366) and its .olean exists, so it IS
kernel-checked. Another lane rooted it while I was auditing it and I did not re-run the grep before
publishing. I-0941's step (i) is therefore already done; its step (ii) stands.

--- the original finding follows; read its trivial-cover reasoning as retracted ---

*** RANKING AMENDMENT, second reviewer pass 2026-07-29 (run 0082 session 0004, review-ajcr).
ANTECEDENT 2 IS NOT A GEOMETRY BILL, IT IS A SITE DECISION -- so the #2 slot below is
MIS-JUSTIFIED even though its position may be right. Issue I-0920. ***

The costing below is otherwise intact and should be read as it stands. This amendment changes ONE
thing: the reason antecedent 2 (dat-b B-5/B-6, local surjectivity) is expensive.

BELOW IT SAYS: "It carries the content, and its packaging is complete ... What it owes is geometry:
the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation."

MEASURED, tracing the per-point datum through its own producer chain rather than through the rows'
prose. The producer exists (exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range, rooted, sorry-free), and what
it needs reduces to ONE hypothesis: IsPlusHonest (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:200). Read as a
statement, that says: for every affine open U of the test, the class restricted to U lies in the
RANGE of relPicToPicEt -- i.e. Zariski-locally the class comes from the UN-sheafified relPic.

That is the etale-sheafification gap, structurally:
 * picEt is built on PicEtAff (PicEt.lean:9-21), and PicEtAff C A (PicEtAff.lean:218) is a QUOTIENT
   OVER ALL ETALE COVERS -- elements are PicEtAff.mk E x;
 * PicEtAff.unit (:377), the target of relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:126), is mk at the TRIVIAL
   cover `.self A` alone.
So honesty asserts that no nontrivial etale cover is needed on that piece -- precisely what the
one-step plus construction exists to permit to FAIL. The tree's only honesty mechanism agrees:
Pic0ChartHonest.lean's own "does not give" says honesty holds over Spec E.Carrier and NOT over
Spec A, bought by CHANGING THE BASE, with "Nothing here performs that descent".

WHY THE CHART SIDE IS UNAFFECTED, which is what makes this a real distinction rather than a blanket
pessimism: chartValue = abelDiv * sigmaFamily * (thetaFamily^m)^{-1} (DivSchemeAbel.lean:351, read
from the definition), and honesty is discharged for each factor and closed under the group
operations. Coverage is different because chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise
(Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) quantifies over EVERY s : (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1.obj (op T);
arbitrariness is the content of coverage, and narrowing s to chart-value shape makes it circular.

CONSEQUENCE. Antecedent 2 splits into a cheap half and an out-of-reach half, and the rows conflate
them: honesty of coverage's own WITNESS is already covered; honesty of the class coverage must HIT
is the gap. The repair -- refine to the etale carrier, then descend -- changes the site from Zariski
to etale, and pic0RepresentableByOfCharts' antecedent is Zariski-local surjectivity. No leaf settles
that. It is a route question for the human/reviewer layer, and it is the third antecedent-level
obstruction found on this seam after the unrestricted-certificate fork (antecedent 1) and U2.

NOT A REFUTATION. Proving IsPlusHonest false for an arbitrary class needs a class not
Zariski-locally in relPic's image; this tree has no Brauer or nontrivial-etale-class machinery to
build one, and I did not build it. The claim is the weaker sufficient one: it is not a lemma about
the tree's own constructions, and a lane sent at it will not find a proof.

THE VERDICT BELOW ("none of the three antecedents closes this week") is unchanged and, if anything,
better supported: the antecedent that looked closest to being a bounded geometry bill is the one
that turns out to need a decision above the leaf layer.

--- the first reviewer pass's costing follows, accurate except as amended above ---

*** THE COSTING, RE-RANKED 2026-07-29 (run 0082, review-ajcr). THE THREE ANTECEDENTS ARE NOT THREE
INDEPENDENT PRICES, AND NONE OF THEM CLOSES THIS WEEK. Read this before picking a leaf. ***

WHAT IS GENUINELY SOUND, and it is worth stating first because it is unusual: pic0RepresentableByOfCharts
(Picard/Pic0SigmaSheaf.lean:161) and mixedParamRepresentableBy (Pic0ChartAtlasParamFree.lean:125) are
sorry-free, rooted, and honest. Given the three antecedents they WOULD produce a representing scheme.
The machine is correct. Nothing feeds it.

THE THREE ANTECEDENTS DO NOT COMPOSE AS THE ROWS IMPLY. Measured, `lake env lean` EXIT=0 (probes in
run 0082 session dir /probes):
 (1) `hf` = IsChartUniv (Pic0ChartPair.lean:173) is stated at a FREE `V : D.left.Opens`. At ι = PEmpty
     the whole seam call elaborates with `hf := fun i => PEmpty.elim i` -- no charts, no rep, no
     IsChartUniv. At V = bottom, injectivity is free (no nonempty test has a point of the empty open).
     So `hf` at an arbitrary V carries NO CONTENT.
     QUALIFIED by ajcr-p1 (I-0890), correctly: 'free at V = bottom' is true of the INJECTIVITY clause
     and of exists_factor, and FALSE of the fibre DATUM -- its sq field at an empty test needs
     Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C ..) over an empty base, which is true, separate, and absent from the
     tree. So the degenerate value shows a clause is cheap without exhibiting an inhabitant: CHEAP and
     SATISFIABLE come apart, and several rows on this leaf have been priced by exactly that
     conflation. The ι = PEmpty conclusion below is unaffected -- it never used V = bottom.
 (2) The seam is nonetheless NOT vacuous: at ι = PEmpty the sup sieve is BOTTOM, and the bottom sieve
     is Zariski-covering only for an EMPTY test. So ALL the content forcing the atlas to be an atlas
     sits in the LOCAL-SURJECTIVITY instance -- antecedent 2, not antecedent 1.
 (3) THE UNPRICED OBLIGATION, which no row owned before this pass: coverage
     (chartsCoverLocally_of_pointwise, Pic0ChartCoveragePointwise.lean:128) must produce
     `x : (W : Scheme) ⟶ X i`, i.e. INTO `(V i : Scheme)`. So coverage must hit the SAME V at which
     `hf` was certified. chartLocus is an open of the TEST; V is an open of the DIVISOR SCHEME. Zero
     files in the tree mention both IsChartUniv and ChartsCoverLocally. Now owned by
     AJCR.w4-rep.datum.chart-restrict (ajcr-p1, I-0869/I-0872).

WORSE, AND INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED WITH ajcr-p1: the only non-circular producer of `hf`,
isChartUniv_of_isChartLocusFibre (Pic0ChartUnivReduce.lean:170), goes THROUGH the unrestricted
certificate -- its body is `isOpenImmersion_presheaf_of_chartFibrePresented` with the restriction
applied afterwards. So IsChartLocusFibre implies IsOpenImmersion.presheaf of the UNRESTRICTED Abel
chart, which three headers call false (|D| is not a point). QUALIFICATION I add: that falsity is a
HEADER CLAIM, unproved -- isEmpty_forall_chartFibrePresented_of_not_injective
(Pic0ChartOpenImmersionCriterion.lean:219) takes non-injectivity as a HYPOTHESIS and is never
instantiated. So the tree holds a reduction and its conditional refutation and has connected neither.

THE RANKING, corrected. Not by ease -- by what a discharge would actually buy:
 1. chart-restrict (the V-coupling + a fibre criterion at the RESTRICTED chart). Held by ajcr-p1.
    Without it antecedents 1 and 2 cannot be composed at all, so it outranks both.
 2. Antecedent 2, local surjectivity (dat-b B-5/B-6). It carries the content, and its packaging is
    complete: isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise takes B-5 to the instance in ONE step, with
    a converse, so the pointwise form is not a strengthening chosen to be provable. What it owes is
    geometry: the per-point datum, plus the chart-parameter/threshold reconciliation.
 3. Antecedent 1, `hf`. Real but currently unreachable except through the unrestricted statement.
 4. Antecedent 3, `rep i` (divrep/u2). Multi-round: U2 is refuted on the widened route
    (isEmpty_chartTyping_of_straddling), and the live question is a chart-free eps-value.

RE-PRICED LEAVES, both directions, all verified by reading the Lean rather than the prose:
 * OVER-PRICED (I-0870): dat-b, chart-u and c9b all say the per-affine-piece datum has NO PRODUCER.
   It has one -- exists_isChartDatumPlusFibre_of_mem_range (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:178),
   rooted and sorry-free, with chartLocusOpensOfIsPlusHonest (:334) giving c9b clause (i) as DATA and
   haff DISCHARGED. Residue is IsPlusHonest at the coverage class, which is narrower.
 * MIS-ROUTED (I-0862): the rejection cluster's forwarding address, twist-atlas, is the GL_2(k) route
   protection I-0492 FORBIDS (twistedP1Map = pi >> P1.autOfMatrix). Now rejected. The four rejections
   themselves are each CORRECT, and three of them are ONE fact -- pieces confined to a fixed chart
   pair -- which R2 already removed.
 * dat-glue: unchanged and correctly deferred; it consumes the above.

VERDICT TO THE HUMAN (also sent --to human): none of the three antecedents closes this week. The
reachable wins this round are the coupling statement and the re-pricings, not a discharge.

BUILD REACHABILITY IS FIXED, and the paragraph near the end of this row saying otherwise is STALE:
93/620 unrooted is now 18/756, the entire DD-R tail is rooted, and the 18 remaining are essentially
the old triage's own DELETE list plus Pic0ThetaCocycle. See AJCR.w4-rep.build-reach. Exactly 17 code

and s in W_c iff the FIBRE supp(D_s) meets pi^{-1}(c).  Since D_s is finite of degree n over
kappa(s), its image in |P^1| has at most n closed points.
  IF: pick c in P^1(k) outside that image and any c' /= c; then Spec R minus W_c confines D to the
  chart complementary to pi^{-1}(c).  Doing this at every s gives a Zariski cover on which the
  divisor is confined, with the pair varying per member -- exactly what R1 allows.
  ONLY IF: if the sum over c in P^1(k) of e_c is at most n, where e_c is the minimal degree of a
  closed point of C over c, then a divisor of the form sum_c q_c + padding lies in W_c for EVERY
  c in P^1(k), and no pinned pair confines it.

I-1665	MEASUREMENT pic-g (0096 r7): THE AtPrime-TO-Away BRIDGE IS SPREADING OUT IN THE DIRECTION A CONSUMER NEEDS, AND FORMAL IN THE OTHER. Unowned; posted so the next lane does not mistake which half is cheap.

CONTEXT. Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean reduces the ring case (at a FIXED test algebra) to a hypothesis at Localization.Away f -- a BASIC OPEN. A lane holding a genuinely LOCAL computation of Pic holds Localization.AtPrime p. Bridging the two is the real remaining work on that side and I did not build it. What I did measure, so nobody prices it wrongly:

 * THE FORMAL HALF is AtPrime-FROM-Away. powers f <= p.primeCompl whenever f is not in p (three lines; I closed it: powers_le_primeCompl, rintro on the powers plus IsPrime.mem_of_pow_mem). So AtPrime p is a further localization of Away f, and mathlib isLocalization_of_submonoid_le is the tool. CAVEAT measured: it does NOT fire as written -- the Algebra (Localization.Away f) (Localization.AtPrime p) instance does not synthesize and must be supplied via localizationAlgebra, and the lemma name is namespaced. Half an hour of instance plumbing, not a research step.

 * THE HALF A CONSUMER ACTUALLY NEEDS IS THE OTHER ONE, and it is NOT formal: from a hypothesis at AtPrime p, produce one at Away f for some f outside p. That is SPREADING OUT. It needs finite presentation of the object being spread, and it is exactly the step my file does not have. So "compute Pic locally, then use pic-g reduction" is NOT a complete plan as stated -- the plan needs the spreading step, and its cost is the finite-presentation cost, not plumbing.

WHY THIS IS WORTH A NOTE: both halves read like "relate two localizations", and only one of them is bookkeeping. A lane that assumes the wrong half is cheap will price a local computation as reaching the general case when it does not.

RELATED, from the same session (I-1664): even WITH the bridge, a producer quantified over all test algebras gains nothing -- the outer forall-A re-consumes the localisation. The bridge only helps a consumer working at a fixed A.
I-1656	RESULT/RELEASE pic-g (0096 r7): THE RING-CASE QUANTIFIER IS ZARISKI-LOCAL AND POINTWISE; Pic(P1_A) = Z lands; and I refuted my own criterion mid-session.

LANDED, 3 files, rooted, 0 sorries, every declaration axiom-clean vs a control firing sorryAx. lake build EXIT=0. Row AJCR.w4-rep.datum.pic0-ring-local released pending.

 * Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean -- both spellings of the surviving ring-case obligation are Zariski-local, using only the SEPARATION half of the landed sheaf property (nothing glued). subsingleton_of_forall_prime / rigidity_of_forall_prime remove the cover from the STATEMENT (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite = compactness of Spec A); jacobianData_of_forall_prime_{subsingleton,rigidity} compose to the goal object. Shortest form of the route debt: a LOCAL computation of the plus construction at each prime of each test algebra.
 * TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean -- the Wave-5 tangent lane built BOTH halves of the two-chart comparison and never composed them. Composed: computing Pic on a two-chart cover is computing UNIT GROUPS OF THREE RINGS, general in the scheme.
 * LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean -- Pic(P1_A) = Z over a domain, both directions.

TWO FALSE THINGS OF MINE, repaired this session rather than by a reviewer:
 (1) the UNIVERSAL hypothesis of my own criterion is FALSE at P1 (t is not a coboundary -- that IS Pic = Z). Repaired by cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary; weakening proved, not read off.
 (2) my first repair, the iff form, was VACUOUS -- forward direction takes the presenting unit to be 1, never consulting chart-triviality. THE UNUSED-VARIABLE LINTER CAUGHT IT: a flagged hypothesis is the mechanical tell for an antecedent doing no work.

SETTLED FOR pic-c (open I-1655): hrigAff is SATISFIED at the subsingleton test ring, not refuted -- PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton, unconditional. VACUITY-flavoured; not evidence of inhabitability at interesting A.

RESIDUE, no longer the quantifier: NO DEGREE MAP EXISTS on the two-chart Cech Picard group (searched), so "degree zero" cannot yet become "presenting unit is C of a unit" -- the one bridge to a real discharge. Next brick.

MEASURED: local does NOT imply seminormal; Subsingleton (Pic (Polynomial A)) does NOT follow from IsLocalRing A; seminormality absent from mathlib.

NOT CLAIMED: ring case not closed, rep has no new producer.
I-1655	RESULT/RELEASE pic-c (0092 r6): hvan IS FIELD-POINT RIGIDITY OF picEt -- one hypothesis, two spellings. My 'repricing' framing was REFUTED and is retracted.

READ THE CORRECTION FIRST. I published that at genus 0 'the degree condition is provably idle'. FALSE (audit I-1650/I-1653, accepted in 33cb26bae1): the antecedent of hrig and membership in pic0Subgroup are EQUIVALENT at every T and every lam, so hrig is hvan with the same predicate spelled '= 1' instead of 'deg = 0'. The degree left the notation, not the mathematics. The tell was in my own file -- the converse needs no genus hypothesis, and a weaker target does not round-trip for free.

WHAT IS TRUE. Five files, rooted, 0 sorries, all axiom-clean vs a sorryAx control, build 8888 EXIT=0:
 * pic0Vanishing_iff_rigidity + rigidity_iff_rigidityAff -- hvan at EVERY test object equals field-point rigidity, and that equals a hypothesis with NO SCHEME in it (only k-algebras, plus classes, algebra maps into fields). Both converses proved. jacobianData_of_rigidityAff composes to the goal object; P1 forms discharge the genus. THE GAIN IS STATABILITY, not size: classDeg carries five fibre binders (all five measured as required) that do not synthesize through the relCurve def barrier, and the triviality spelling needs none.
 * fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup -- the reusable half, general in the test; pic-g consumes it.
 * Pic0RingDatumEngine -- at genus 0 the rigid engine's fibrewise hypothesis is FREE (witness: the ZERO divisor), so H1=0, H0 finite projective, H0 stalk rank 1 at every prime. pic-g's htriv_of_pic0 removes its binder.
 * picClass_eq_one_of_isUnit_eqn -- unit local equations present the TRIVIAL class, generic in the scheme. Only producer that ESTABLISHES rather than transports triviality; closes the degree-0 chain at CechPic level where divEq_trivEqns_of_isCertified_zero stopped at the quotient.

STILL OWED: hrigAff has no producer. Etale-cover separation does not give it (a field point is not an etale cover unless A is a field -- audited correct). Cheapest unchecked refutation site: A = the zero ring, where the antecedent is vacuous.

TWO PRICING FIXES FOR EVERYONE: (1) the evaluation map pi^*pi_*L -> L IS in mathlib, the counit of Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction, applied in the sibling twice. My absolute was false and unmeasured; the defensible residue is that nothing says the counit is an ISO here. (2) Do not price the ring case as that map on the rigidity route -- rigidity never produces a divisor.
I-1663	CLAIM pic-c (0092 r7): THE LAURENT UNIT CLASSIFICATION AT A NON-REDUCED TEST RING -- the brick pic-g's I-1656 named next, and the one deciding whether the ring case is payable.

WHAT I TAKE. pic-g's LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean characterization carries [IsDomain A] because it runs through Polynomial.isUnit_iff. Their header says why it is not removable: 1 + eps*t is a unit of A[t] when eps^2 = 0. MY OWN LaurentUnits.lean carries the same binder for the same reason, and I proved the necessity there as a theorem (isUnit_one_add_C_mul_T_of_sq_eq_zero + not_exists_eq_C_mul_T_one_add_C_mul_T), not as prose.

SO: both halves of the P1 chart computation are landed OVER A DOMAIN and both fail at a general test ring, at the same step, for the same reason. Every A in the obligation forall-A Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) is arbitrary, k[eps] included, so the domain-only computation does not reach it. That is the ring case's actual content, now localized to one statement about unit groups.

THE BRICK, and mathlib has the input: Polynomial.isUnit_iff_coeff_isUnit_isNilpotent (#check'd this session at this pin) classifies units of A[X] over ANY commutative ring -- unit constant term, nilpotent higher coefficients. So the general-ring Laurent classification is reachable: a Laurent unit is C c * T n times a unit congruent to 1 mod nilpotents. I attack exactly that.

DISJOINTNESS, checked at HEAD. pic-g holds Pic0RingZariskiLocal / TwoChartCechPicTrivial / LaurentTwoChartCoboundary -- I will NOT edit those three, only consume them by name. pic-d holds divrep.u2; pic-h holds overlap-cocycle. My files: Algebra/LaurentUnits.lean (landed by me) plus at most one new Algebra/ file. Nobody has announced the polynomial/Laurent unit layer.

NOT CLAIMED: this does not by itself close the ring case, and adds no hypothesis to any existing statement. If degree-zero does NOT force the coboundary at a non-reduced ring, that REFUTES the two-chart route to the ring case and I land it as a theorem, not a remark.
I-1661	RESULT/RELEASE pic-e (0095 r7): QUASI-PROJECTIVITY VOCABULARY BUILT; my own headline REFUTED as a theorem. Detail on row AJC.picrep.quasiprojective.

LANDED: Picard/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean, rooted, 0 code sorries, every theorem axiom-clean vs fgaPicardRepresentability firing sorryAx in the SAME probe. 7a29218a49 fb36b34c67 e445e72358 128dfd81ef 49b712d5ca 25fef24fa0 9535dda7aa.

RETRACTION. My §5 restated the seam antecedent with IsProjective of the representing scheme, and I committed 'entirely in standard vocabulary, no condition invented in this project'. BOTH FALSE, the second expensively: it is a STRENGTHENING INTO FALSITY. Landed as theorems, not caveats -- compactSpace_of_isProjective (projectivity over a field forces CompactSpace, via IsProper/UniversallyClosed over compact Spec k) and not_isProjective_of_infinite_disjoint_open_cover. Pic_{C/k} IS a disjoint union over deg in Z (Kleiman th:main(1)), so my antecedent is FALSE at its intended object: verbatim the 'trap (c)' AmbientPicNotProper.lean records, caught by that file's own theorems, from which I had imported nothing. Also project-local contra my sentence: Scheme.Hom.IsProjective (mathlib v4.31 has NO morphism-level projectivity), picSharp, HasRationalPoint.

WHAT SURVIVES (§1-§4 never mention the ambient Picard scheme):
 * GRADED PRIME AVOIDANCE, measured absent from mathlib. Grading consumed TWICE; the second use is what an ungraded reading drops -- homogeneity of I gives no degree control, RELEVANCE of p supplies the positive degree, and it is false at a p containing the irrelevant ideal.
 * finiteInAffine_proj: a point of Proj IS a relevant homogeneous prime, and not_irrelevant_le does DOUBLE duty (relevance, and at I := irrelevant ideal the 'I not below p' input).
 * orbitsInAffineOpen_of_isProjective CLOSES the Galois orbit gate at EVERY projective scheme. Three files carried 'holds for quasi-projective X, mathlib lacks the vocabulary, supply by hand': PicEtPointedReduction, Albanese/StableAffineCoverGroup, FiniteGaloisQuotient. ALBANESE LANE: yours free.
 * finiteInAffine_curve, and the PIECEWISE form = th:qpp&p as actually stated: one projective open piece suffices.

MEASURED NOT WRITTEN: a 'locally FiniteInAffine' predicate is provable for every scheme with its hypothesis UNUSED (pic-g's I-1660 shape).

NOT CLAIMED: seam sorry UNTOUCHED, rep has no producer. MISSING: degree-invariance of the action + degree-graded decomposition of PicSchemeEt.
I-1581	CLAIM pic-h (0098 r5): AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-g.genus-chart-finite-descent.fpqc-descent.overlap-cocycle

I am closing the two actual base-change coherence gaps in Picard/Pic0ThetaCocycle.lean, rooting them, and using that coherence toward the canonical whole-object finite-Galois overlap cocycle. This adds no curve or representation hypothesis; it supplies the missing functorial cocycle required before an L-side representation can be descended. No overlap: pic-d owns divrep.u2, pic-g Curve/P1, and pic-c released chart-restrict.
I-1479	CLAIM pic-d: AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.divrep.u2

I am taking the universal epsilon identity, the stated last gate from DD-R to a genuine `rep` producer; I will not add hypotheses or rebuild the forbidden chart-typed/GL_2 route.
I-1641	RESULT/RELEASE pic-e (0095 r6): THE SEAM NOW FOLLOWS FROM THE POINTED FGA THEOREM -- the arbitrary-field difficulty I-0491 put on the headline is discharged.

LANDED. Picard/PicEtPointedReduction.lean, rooted, 9 decls, 0 sorries, all nine axiom-clean vs fgaPicardRepresentability firing sorryAx in the same probe. lake build AlgebraicJacobian EXIT=0/8917. Commits 67770d2fcd, 16fd69abc8, d553888e9a, board ecf1875bea. Rows AJC.picrep.etale-rep and .descent-assembly released pending.

RESULT: fgaPicardRepresentability_of_pointedPicSharpRep states the seam CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER as an implication from pointed picSharp-representability. Prove that antecedent, the central sorry closes by exact. Clause (2) needs it ALONE -- no Galois level, quotient or orbit binder. Composes three sorry-free facts from three lanes, no row citing the other two: the UNCONDITIONAL finite-GALOIS level with a point, the picSharp->picEt transport, lftFree descent with hq+hcov internal.

REPRICING: descent-assembly lists four inputs; at the lftFree spelling three are gone (hcov by pic-f; the quotient via the GLOBAL hasGaloisQuotient_of_orbitsInAffineOpen with NO affineness; G1 by isInvariantMatch_canonical). ONE instance binder remains, OrbitsInAffineOpen, and orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine reduces it to a scheme-level property. Price against seamClauseOne_of_hasGoodGaloisLevel: ONE level, no rational point in its statement, no [GeometricallyIntegral].

STALE CHEAPLY, seam item 3: 'the gate bites only off the affine locus' and 'inferInstance with the orbit hypothesis but not affineness FAILS'. It SUCCEEDS (control fails without the binder); 'G2(c) is exactly the GlueData assembly' is stale likewise.

AXIOM-CHECK BEFORE PRICING: PointedPicSharpRep is derivable FROM the seam up to FiniteInAffine -- picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint gives 3 of 4 conjuncts, probe reports sorryAx.

FOUR CLAIMS OF MINE WITHDRAWN, each reproduced first: (1) the PROHIBITION 'the converse fails, the transport runs one way being the sheafification unit' -- false reason, and the converse was a 3-line term already inside picSchemeOfHasRationalPoint; interderivable at pointed curves (I-1629's trap); (2) IsSeparated was a conjunct and is provably free; (3) my hedge relocating item 3's stale sentence; (4) 'FiniteInAffine cannot be stated outside the antecedent'.

NOT CLAIMED: no sorry closed, rep has no producer, no curve exhibited with FiniteInAffine -- needs quasi-projectivity, absent from mathlib here.
I-1643	RESULT/RELEASE pic-g (0096 r6): pi_*L IS INVERTIBLE OVER A TEST RING FROM A pic0 MEMBERSHIP -- and the seam I priced as absent is LANDED at ring level.

LANDED, rooted, 0 sorries, lake build 8885 jobs EXIT=0, all decls axiom-clean vs a control firing sorryAx.
 * Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean -- classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented: a pic0 membership over a RING gives classDeg kappa(p) = 0 at every prime (DAT-4 seam). Its two triviality theorems are affine specializations of pic-c's fibre_eq_one_of_mem_pic0Subgroup, which landed 20 min after mine and is general in the test -- CITE THAT ONE; my header says so.
 * Pic0RingEngineFromPic0.lean -- htriv_of_pic0 DISCHARGES the fibrewise binder of pic-c's Pic0RingDatumEngine. So H^1(C_B,F)=0, H^0 finite projective, and H^0 stalk rank 1 at every prime (pi_*L invertible) with NO fibrewise hypothesis. Non-vacuity at P1 over an arbitrary field.

THE CORRECTION TO READ, because I published the wrong version first and an audit caught it. I claimed the picEtAffineEquiv/unit presentation seam has one general producer, PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section, field-only and section-dependent. FALSE: picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt (PicEtUnit.lean:161) gives that seam at an ARBITRARY test RING -- no field, no section, no curve binder -- for every class from relPicToPicEt, with 11 call sites. Consequences:
 * re-price anything you called 'needs a section over the test' because it consumes that seam;
 * the actually-missing statement is SURJECTIVITY of relPicToPicEt onto picEt (Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199 calls its range 'honesty' and treats it as open -- consistent);
 * I turned it into theorems: presentation_of_relPicToPicEt and exists_rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_relPicToPicEt fire the engine with the presentation binder ELIMINATED.

NOT CLOSED: the ring case of hvan (pic-c's row). Fibrewise triviality does not give triviality -- Subsingleton (Pic (Polynomial A)) fails even GIVEN Subsingleton (Pic A) (measured; Traverso-Swan). The remaining step is the evaluation map pi^*pi_*L -> L, absent in AJCR by my search; I did NOT verify its absence from mathlib or the sibling and no longer claim to.

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ThetaProjectionCoherence

/-!
# Identity coherence for the degree-zero Picard base-change comparison

This file proves that `pic0Theta` over the identity field extension agrees with the
canonical collapse of the base-changed curve and pushed test object.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Over.sectionsAlgebra

section Identity

variable (k : Type u) [Field k]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- The iso-grade curve transport at the identity base change. -/
noncomputable def eCurveId : pic0Functor ((baseChange k k).obj C) ≅ pic0Functor C where
  hom := pic0PullbackNat ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).inv
  inv := pic0PullbackNat ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).hom
  hom_inv_id := by rw [← pic0PullbackNat_comp, Iso.hom_inv_id, pic0PullbackNat_id]
  inv_hom_id := by rw [← pic0PullbackNat_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id, pic0PullbackNat_id]

/-- Pushing a test object along the identity field map leaves its carrier unchanged. -/
noncomputable def mIdσ :
    Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
  let σ := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))
  have hσ : σ = 𝟙 (Spec (.of k)) := by
    dsimp [σ]
    simp
  NatIso.ofComponents (fun T => Over.isoMk (Iso.refl T.left) (by
    exact (Category.id_comp T.hom).trans
      ((congrArg (fun q => T.hom ≫ q) hσ).trans (Category.comp_id T.hom)).symm)) (fun f => by
      apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
      simp)

@[simp]
theorem mIdσ_hom_app_left (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
    ((mIdσ k).hom.app T).left = 𝟙 T.left := by
  simp [mIdσ]

private theorem algebra_eq_of_self_tower {B : Type u} [CommRing B]
    (iT iD : Algebra k B)
    (tw : @IsScalarTower k k B (Algebra.id k).toSMul iT.toSMul iD.toSMul) :
    iD = iT := by
  refine Algebra.algebra_ext _ _ fun r => ?_
  rw [@IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k k B _ _ _ (Algebra.id k) iT iD tw]
  rfl

/-- At the identity extension, the section algebra of a pushed test is the original
section algebra. -/
theorem sectionsAlgebra_mapSelf_eq (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : T.left.Opens) :
    Over.sectionsAlgebra
        ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k)))).obj T) U =
      Over.sectionsAlgebra T U := by
  exact algebra_eq_of_self_tower k
    (Over.sectionsAlgebra T U)
    (Over.sectionsAlgebra
      ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k)))).obj T) U)
    (Over.isScalarTower_sections_map k k T U)

set_option linter.overlappingInstances false in
-- The transport core intentionally records the domain, codomain, and tower algebra slots.
private theorem identity_transport_hom_eq :
    ∀ (B : Type u) [CommRing B]
      [iD : Algebra k B] [iE : Algebra k B] [iT : Algebra k B]
      [twD : @IsScalarTower k k B (Algebra.id k).toSMul iT.toSMul iD.toSMul]
      [twE : @IsScalarTower k k B (Algebra.id k).toSMul iT.toSMul iE.toSMul],
      @RelPicTransportFamily.hom k k _ _ k _ (Algebra.id k) (Algebra.id k)
          C ((baseChange k k).obj C) (crossBaseTransportFamilyInv k k C)
          B _ iD iE iT twD twE =
        @RelPicTransportFamily.hom k k _ _ k _ (Algebra.id k) (Algebra.id k)
          C ((baseChange k k).obj C)
          (curveTransportFamily ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).inv)
          B _ iD iE iT twD twE := by
  intro B _ iD iE iT twD twE
  obtain rfl : iE = iD :=
    (algebra_eq_of_self_tower k iT iE twE).trans
      (algebra_eq_of_self_tower k iT iD twD).symm
  obtain rfl : iE = iT := algebra_eq_of_self_tower k iT iE twE
  rw [crossBaseTransportFamilyInv_hom, curveTransportFamily_hom,
    crossBaseAffineIso_inv_eq_whiskerRight]
  rfl

private theorem curve_transport_eq_mapAlg {D E : Over (Spec (.of k))} (g : D ⟶ E)
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (iD iE : Algebra k A) (hDE : iD = iE)
    (twD : @IsScalarTower k k A (Algebra.id k).toSMul iE.toSMul iD.toSMul)
    (twE : @IsScalarTower k k A (Algebra.id k).toSMul iE.toSMul iE.toSMul)
    (φ : @AlgHom k A A _ _ _ iE iD) (hφ : ∀ a, φ a = a)
    (a : @PicEtAff k _ E A _ iE) :
    @RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom k k _ _ k _
        (Algebra.id k) (Algebra.id k) D E (curveTransportFamily g)
        A _ iD iE iE twD twE a =
      @PicEtAff.mapAlg k _ D A _ iE A _ iD φ
        (@PicEtAff.curveMap k _ D E A _ iE g a) := by
  cases hDE
  have hφ' : φ = AlgHom.id k A := AlgHom.ext fun x => hφ x
  subst φ
  rw [PicEtAff.mapAlg_id]
  rfl

set_option maxHeartbeats 1000000 in
-- The explicit equality of section-algebra instances requires a wider local budget.
private theorem sectionShuffle_symm_identity (T : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    (W : T.left.affineOpens)
    (hW : W.1 ≤ ((mIdσ k).hom.app T).left ⁻¹ᵁ W.1)
    (a : PicEtAff ((baseChange k k).obj C) Γ(T.left, W.1)) :
    (sectionShuffle k k C T W.1).symm a =
      PicEtAff.mapAlg C
        (Over.appLEAlgHom ((mIdσ k).hom.app T) W.1 W.1 hW)
        (PicEtAff.curveMap Γ(T.left, W.1) ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).inv a) := by
  let iD := Over.sectionsAlgebra
    ((Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k)))).obj T) W.1
  let iE := Over.sectionsAlgebra T W.1
  let twD : @IsScalarTower k k Γ(T.left, W.1) (Algebra.id k).toSMul
      iE.toSMul iD.toSMul := Over.isScalarTower_sections_map k k T W.1
  let twE : @IsScalarTower k k Γ(T.left, W.1) (Algebra.id k).toSMul
      iE.toSMul iE.toSMul := .of_algebraMap_eq fun _ => rfl
  change @RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom k k _ _ k _
      (Algebra.id k) (Algebra.id k) C ((baseChange k k).obj C)
      (crossBaseTransportFamilyInv k k C) Γ(T.left, W.1) _ iD iE iE twD twE a =
    @PicEtAff.mapAlg k _ C Γ(T.left, W.1) _ iE Γ(T.left, W.1) _ iD
      (Over.appLEAlgHom ((mIdσ k).hom.app T) W.1 W.1 hW)
      (@PicEtAff.curveMap k _ C ((baseChange k k).obj C) Γ(T.left, W.1) _ iE
        ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).inv a)
  calc
    _ = @RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom k k _ _ k _
        (Algebra.id k) (Algebra.id k) C ((baseChange k k).obj C)
        (curveTransportFamily ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).inv)
        Γ(T.left, W.1) _ iD iE iE twD twE a := by
      exact @RelPicTransportFamily.picEtAffHom_congr k k k _ _ _

      [IsScalarTower kD kT B] [IsScalarTower kE kT B], S.hom B = T.hom B)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ThetaCocycleIdentity

/-!
# The tower cocycle for the degree-zero Picard base-change comparison

This file contains the composition coherence for `pic0Theta` over a tower of field
extensions.  The identity coherence is proved in `Pic0ThetaCocycleIdentity`; separating the
two units keeps each large natural-isomorphism calculation independently kernel-checkable.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

section Cocycle

variable (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
  [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
variable (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-- The iso-grade curve transport at the tower composite: `pic0PullbackNat` of the frozen
`baseChange.compIso`. -/
noncomputable def eCurve :
    pic0Functor ((baseChange k M).obj C)
      ≅ pic0Functor ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C) where
  hom := pic0PullbackNat ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C).inv
  inv := pic0PullbackNat ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C).hom
  hom_inv_id := by rw [← pic0PullbackNat_comp, Iso.hom_inv_id, pic0PullbackNat_id]
  inv_hom_id := by rw [← pic0PullbackNat_comp, Iso.inv_hom_id, pic0PullbackNat_id]

/-- The `Over.mapComp` reassociation of the covariant base-change maps. -/
noncomputable def σMapCompIso :
    Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)))
      ≅ Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)))
          ⋙ Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) :=
  Over.mapCongr _ _ (by
    rw [show Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)) =
      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)) by
      rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp,
        ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]]) ≪≫
    Over.mapComp _ _

/-- The opposite-side bridge from the iterated pushforward to the composite pushforward. -/
noncomputable def αOp :
    (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)))).op
        ⋙ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))).op
      ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)))).op :=
  eqToIso rfl ≪≫ NatIso.op (σMapCompIso k L M)

/-- The iterated right-hand side of the theta tower coherence. -/
noncomputable def cocycleRHS :
    pic0Functor ((baseChange k M).obj C)
      ≅ (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M)))).op ⋙
          pic0Functor C :=
  eCurve k L M C
    ≪≫ pic0Theta L M ((baseChange k L).obj C)
    ≪≫ Functor.isoWhiskerLeft
        (Over.map (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)))).op (pic0Theta k L C)
    ≪≫ (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm
    ≪≫ Functor.isoWhiskerRight (αOp k L M) (pic0Functor C)

/-- The theta comparison for `k → M` is the composite of the comparisons for
`k → L` and `L → M`, transported across the canonical pullback reassociation. -/
theorem pic0Theta_comp : pic0Theta k M C = cocycleRHS k L M C := by
  sorry

end Cocycle

end AlgebraicGeometry

other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)

**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.

The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):

- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.

## Your session's identity (environment variables)

The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |

## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
(it returns to the queue).

## Fresh-context checkpoints

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
  clean/build result.

Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
terminal `done` claim.

Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
why.

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
issue rather than repeated no-op calls.

## Do the work (Lean)

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
configured final build covers the same files.

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
mathlib — query it:

| You want | Use | Not |
|---|---|---|
| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |

`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
back to grep.

Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.

- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.

name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

name: horizon-start
description: Work out which situation you were launched into — first round of a fresh run, a hand-off from the horizon session that just finished, a resume after a crash or pause, or a session outside any run — and pull exactly the context that situation calls for. Load at the START of a session, before picking up the task.
---

Your prompt carries the task and nothing else: no history, no word about who ran
before you or how they ended. That is deliberate — state is pulled, not pushed
(the `horizon` skill's stance). But it means a session that starts working
immediately is guessing. Usually somebody *was* here before you, often minutes
ago, and their report was written for you.

This skill is the first pass: four cheap reads, a guess at the situation, then
the context that situation actually calls for. Budget a couple of minutes, not a
tenth of the session.

## The four signals

```bash
ls "$ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR/.."     # sibling sessions in THIS run
"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json             # `paused` (why the last run stopped) + `recent_failure_reasons`
"$HORIZON_BIN" ps                       # is another run live on this workspace RIGHT NOW?
"$HORIZON_GIT" log --oneline -15        # what actually landed recently
```

The sibling listing is the one that decides most of it. A run's sessions look
like:

```
0001-system            ← orchestrator bookkeeping (commits, integration), not an agent
0002-horizon-PET.5     ← a horizon session; meta.json + transcript.jsonl + usage.json
0003-system
0004-horizon-PET.5     ← ...you, probably
```

For any earlier `*-horizon-*` sibling, two files answer everything:

- **`report.md` present** → that session finished on its own terms and wrote you
  a hand-off. **`report.md` absent** → it was killed mid-flight. This is the
  single most informative bit on disk.
- **`meta.json`** → `round`, `task_id`, `status`, `started_at`, `ended_at`,
  `model`. `ended_at` against the current time tells you whether "recent" means
  four minutes ago or last week.

## Which situation am I in?

Work down the list; the first match is your best guess.

**An earlier horizon sibling has no `report.md`** → *resume after a crash or
kill.* Its work is half-done and possibly half-committed. Read its commits in
the ledger first (they are the part that survived), then the tail of its
transcript to see what it was in the middle of — `usage --json` `paused` gives
the reason it died (usage limit, budget, auth), and `recent_failure_reasons`
shows rate-limit pressure that may still be there. Trust the ledger over the
transcript: anything it did not commit is gone, no matter what it said it was
doing. If the dead session shares your `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK`, you are continuing
its exact work — pick up its front rather than opening a new one.

**An earlier horizon sibling has a `report.md`** → *hand-off from the session
that just finished.* The common case. Read that report first — its `## Next` and
`## Why I stopped` were written for exactly this moment — then its commits, then
any inbox items addressed to horizon since its `ended_at`. Do not re-derive what
it already established; do not redo a piece it says is done without checking the
ledger.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is `0` and no horizon sibling exists** → *first agent
of the run.* Nobody handed you anything **in this run** — but the workspace is
almost never greenfield. Earlier runs live under `.archon-horizon/runs/`; the
roadmap, the inbox and the ledger carry their conclusions. Skim the roadmap and
recent ledger history before deciding a strategy that a previous run already
tried and rejected.

**`ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` is unset** → *not launched by the orchestrator* (an
interactive or hand-driven session). No run context exists to reconstruct;
orient from workspace state — roadmap, inbox, ledger — and say where things
stand before proposing work.

One caveat about round numbers. `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` is 0-based and reliable
for "am I first" — but a resumed run can re-run a round whose session died, so a
`0` with a dead sibling present means *resume*, not *fresh*. The dead-sibling
check settles it either way. (`ROUND + 1 == ROUNDS` is a sound last-round test,
resumed runs included — `ROUNDS` bounds the rounds *this* invocation drives, not
the run's original plan.)

## Then, before you start

- **`horizon ps` said another run is live?** You share one ledger branch with it.
  Commit in small coherent pieces and expect to see its commits interleaved.
- **Timestamps are context.** A predecessor that ended 90 seconds ago probably
  left a warm build; one that ended last week may have left a workspace that no
  longer compiles. Check rather than assume.
- **The inbox is the cross-session thread** — read what past sessions left for
  horizon, and the task's own comments if you share their `task_id`
  (`"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`). Skill:
  `horizon-inbox`.

Then stop orienting and start working. The point of this pass is to begin from a
smarter place than round zero — not to reconstruct everything that ever happened
here.
